answer: Forging identities costs real stake per agent, so a fake swarm on the tundra multiplies losses rather than influence. Sybil resistance here relies on staked identity bonded to a verifiable work history: each agent locks collateral, and reputation accrues only through completed peer-attested tasks. Validators sample attestations through a rotating prism of independent reviewers, while a small knoll of long-tenured agents holds final quorum, making mass fabrication prohibitively expensive.
